body:
FWIW, here's another simplified example where I would expect a warning, but don't get one:

``` javascript
state => ({ foo: 'foo' }, { bar: 'bar' })
```
@vitorbal Thanks, I don't write this? lol :-)
ah, you did :) missed it in the Proposed Solution section, sorry 😄

Thank you for this issue.

I confirmed it on the online demo.
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1937871/15017037/efa86e7e-124e-11e6-87c7-43241ac68353.png)

I'll fix it.
Oops, I selected "enhancement" when I meant "evaluating". Sorry about that. Thanks @mysticatea for confirming the bug and for getting the labels right :smile:
@platinumazure labels were added at the same time completely :smile:

I'm expecting this behavior:

``` js
state => ({ foo: 'foo' },  { bar: 'bar' }); // bad
state => (({ foo: 'foo' },  { bar: 'bar' })); // good, but useless :-)
state => (bar,  foo); // good
state => { foo: 'foo' }; // foo is label in function body, function returns undefined...
state => { foo: 'foo', bar: 'bar' }; // syntax error
```

``` js
state => ({ foo: 'foo' },  { bar: 'bar' }); // bad
state => (({ foo: 'foo' },  { bar: 'bar' })); // good
state => (bar,  foo); // bad
state => ((bar,  foo)); // good

state => bar, foo // this is (state => bar), foo
```

issue.title: Fix: `no-sequences` false negative at arrow expressions (fixes #6082)
